title: Operability Thermostat — compact control surface for GPU pool scaling & burst policies
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design a compact, single-pane control surface (the 'Operability Thermostat') that lets SREs and platform engineers view GPU pool health and adjust autoscaling and burst parameters with minimal cognitive load. Goal: embed realtime health signals, safe guardrails, and quick rollback controls into a micro-interaction-driven panel that fits inside the Dedicated Capacity pool detail page. Deliverables: high-fidelity Figma screens, interactive prototype, redlines, accessibility checklist, and handoff tokens.
acceptance_criteria: Single-pane component displays CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth, p99 latency, and token throughput
Scaling policy editor supports target-based and schedule-based rules and preview of expected concurrency changes
Burst configuration includes burst budget meter, manual burst trigger, and automatic cooldown with visible rollback
Component fits 980px container width and matches console typography tokens
QA checklist passed: keyboard navigable, color contrast >= 4.5:1, aria labels for dynamic charts
comments: 2026-02-26 Aisha Patel: Initial concept sketches uploaded to Figma. Focus on reducing cognitive load for on-call.
2026-03-01 Jordan Kim: Engineering review — prefers separate edit modal for complex schedule rules to avoid accidental changes. Asked for API contract example.
2026-03-02 Mateo Ruiz (Eng): Provided mock API payload for scaling policies: /pools/:id/policies. Noted validation needed for overlapping schedules.
2026-03-03 PM review (Leah Santos): Request to surface cost delta estimate when changing autoscale targets to aid product decisioning.
2026-03-04 Design critique: adjust burst meter color scale; change 'Enable burst' toggle to two-step enable (confirm small budget) to prevent accidental spend.
2026-03-05 Aisha Patel: Updated prototype with schedule modal and cost-delta preview. Requesting final design review before handoff.
notes: Trade-offs: compact UI sacrifices detailed timeline — we rely on drill-in modal for full history.
Consideration: expose a 'safety bar' that prevents target > 2x current baseline without explicit approval for enterprise tenants.
Follow-ups: telemetry events proposal to capture 'manual_burst_trigger' and 'scaling_policy_change' for cost analytics.
